elicitation_input.question: where are mucosal associated lymphoid tissues present in the human body and why

llm_generation.text:
Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) is found beneath mucosal surfaces, including the gastrointestinal tract (tonsils, appendix, and small intestine), oral and nasopharyngeal passages, lungs, salivary glands, thyroid, breast, eye, and skin.  

It is present at these sites because mucosal surfaces are major entry points for antigens and infectious agents. MALT provides a first line of immune defense by detecting these antigens and mounting appropriate local immune responses while helping maintain tolerance to food and commensal bacteria.
